lessons.title: Story Time: Racing Against Time
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss time-related events in a story.
success_criteria: I can say what time something happened.
I can say why time mattered in the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss times when being on time matters.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a story where time plays an important role, modelling discussion of time-related events.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions about the time-related events in the story.
key_questions: What time did this happen?
Why did time matter here?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of time-related events — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time when being on time mattered to your family.

lessons.title: Telling Time in 5-Minute Intervals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to tell the time to 5-minute intervals.
success_criteria: I can read times like 'five past' and 'ten past'.
I can show these times on a clock.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap quarter hour times from Week 8.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce reading times in 5-minute intervals (five past, ten past, twenty to, etc.) using a demonstration clock.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise reading and setting 5-minute interval times.
key_questions: What time does this clock show?
Can you show me twenty-five past 3?

differentiation.support: Focus on five and ten past/to only

lessons.assessment_notes: Record introduction of 5-minute interval time-telling, a key Year 2 objective — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Practise telling the time in 5-minute intervals at home.

lessons.title: Writing a Detailed Daily Timetable
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a timetable using 5-minute interval times.
success_criteria: I can write times in 5-minute intervals.
I can describe an activity for each time.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a detailed timetable using 5-minute interval times.
lessons.independent_task: Children write their own detailed timetable using 5-minute interval times.
key_questions: What time does this activity start?
Can you write it using 5-minute intervals?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a detailed timetable with several precise time points

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of 5-minute interval time vocabulary to writing — evidence for ENG.W2/MATHS.MEA links.
lessons.plenary: Share detailed timetables with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Make a detailed timetable for your day.

lessons.title: Comparing Durations to 5 Minutes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to calculate simple durations using 5-minute intervals.
success_criteria: I can say how long between two times.
I can use 5-minute intervals.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model calculating the duration between two 5-minute interval times.
lessons.independent_task: Children calculate durations between given times, showing working.
key_questions: How long between these two times?
How did you work it out?

differentiation.support: Use a clock face to count on

lessons.assessment_notes: Record duration calculation using 5-minute intervals, extending Year 2 skills — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Calculate a duration between two times at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Clock and Time Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read clock/time-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read time words.
I can read a sentence about time.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to time-themed words (e.g. 'minute', 'hour', 'clock').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading time words over the week.

lessons.title: Time Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve word problems involving time.
success_criteria: I can solve a time word problem.
I can show my working using a clock face.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems involving time (e.g. 'the film starts at 3:15 and lasts 45 minutes, what time does it end?').
lessons.independent_task: Children solve time word problems, showing working with a clock face.
key_questions: What time does the film end?
How did you work it out?

differentiation.support: Use a clock face to count on

lessons.assessment_notes: Record time word problem solving skill, an advanced Year 2 objective — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a time word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Explaining My Timetable
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain their detailed timetable clearly.
success_criteria: I can explain the times on my timetable.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear explanation of a detailed timetable.
lessons.independent_task: Children explain their timetable to a small group, answering a question.
key_questions: What happens at this time?
Can you answer a question about your timetable?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and time vocabulary application — evidence for ENG.SL1/MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Explain your timetable to your family.

lessons.title: Time Consolidation: Mixed Practice
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply a full range of time-telling skills confidently.
success_criteria: I can tell the time to 5-minute intervals.
I can calculate durations.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's time-telling and duration skills.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a mixed time consolidation activity.
key_questions: What time is this?
How long between these times?

differentiation.support: Complete with reduced complexity and support

lessons.assessment_notes: Consolidation check on 5-minute interval time-telling before Friday's review — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate progress in telling the time this week.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising telling the time over the week.

lessons.title: Telling Time Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions linked to time.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage involving time, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What time did the event happen?
Why might knowing the time matter here?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on time facts.

lessons.title: Telling Time Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise and confidently apply 5-minute interval time-telling.
success_criteria: I can tell the time to 5-minute intervals confidently.
I can calculate simple durations.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole week's time learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering the week's time skills.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a final review worksheet on telling time to 5-minute intervals.
key_questions: What have we learned about telling the time?
What was tricky at first but easier now?

differentiation.support: Word bank and clock face support provided
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain time calculations in detail independently

lessons.assessment_notes: End of Telling Time unit consolidation summary for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's telling time learning.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising telling the time with your family.
